components.css: .ds-course-card { border-radius: 18px; width: 250px; background-color: #ffffff; outline: 1.5px solid #d7deea; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(23,29,51,0.06); transition: outline-color 0.2s ease, box-shadow 0.2s ease; } .ds-course-card:hover { outline-color: #f6a355; box-shadow: 0 10px 24px rgba(229,114,0,0.14); } .ds-course-card-body { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; padding: 14px 16px; font-weight: 500; font-size: 15px; color: #171d33; } .ds-course-rating { align-self: flex-start; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 700; color: #c25f00; background: #fef3e8; border-radius: 999px; padding: 3px 9px; } .ds-course-details-btn { width: 100%; height: 34px; border-radius: 10px; border: 1px solid #d7deea; background-color: #eef1f7; color: #232d4b; font-weight: 600; font-size: 13px; transition: background-color 0.15s ease, border-color 0.15s ease; } .ds-course-details-btn:hover { background-color: #232d4b; border-color: #232d4b; color: #ffffff; }

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Modal primary action button, solid Jefferson Blue.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { height: 38px; padding: 0 18px; border-radius: 10px; font-weight: 700; font-size: 13px; background: #232d4b; border: 1px solid #232d4b; color: #ffffff; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s ease, border-color 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover, .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { background: #171d33; border-color: #171d33; outline: 2px solid #e57200; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Modal secondary/ghost action button; hover turns orange rather than deepening blue.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { height: 38px; padding: 0 18px; border-radius: 10px; font-weight: 700; font-size: 13px; background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e1e4e8; color: #565d6b; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.15s ease, color 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover, .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { border-color: #f6a355; color: #9c4c00; outline: 2px solid #e57200; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Tag / Rating Pill
components.description: Full-pill badge, tinted background with matching dark text of the same hue; used for ratings, tags, course-code badges.
components.css: .ds-pill { display: inline-block; border-radius: 999px; padding: 4px 10px; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; } .ds-pill--blue { background: #eef1f7; color: #232d4b; } .ds-pill--orange { background: #fef3e8; color: #c25f00; }

narrative.overview:
This is a light, institutional-but-legible system built for reading a prerequisite graph at a glance: a near-white canvas carries the weight, and two UVA hues do the semantic work of telling a student where they are and what's connected. Jefferson Blue is the structural, wayfinding color (chrome, edges, secondary emphasis); Cavalier Orange is reserved for "you are here" — the active course, the current focus, the thing demanding attention. Both hues are used as graduated 8-10 step ramps rather than flat swatches, so the same two colors can carry a card's border, a pill's fill, a heading's ink, and a button's hover state without ever feeling like a single flat brand stripe.

The system is currently proven end-to-end only on the Explore page and its NodeDetails/CourseMiniGraph popup; Sidebar picked up matching nav states. Home and Login have not been visually rebuilt and should not be treated as evidence of a different world — they simply haven't adopted this one yet.
keyCharacteristics: Light neutral ground (white/near-white/warm gray) with color reserved for meaning, not decoration
Two hues, each as a graduated tint/shade ramp, never used flat
Pill-shaped tags and rounded-rectangle cards throughout; no sharp corners
Soft, colored (not black) shadows tied to the nearby accent
Orange = active/focus/"you are here"; Blue = structural/connected/"related to it"

rules.name: The Two-Hue Ramp Rule
rules.body: Every color in the system traces back to UVA orange, UVA blue, or a neutral gray step — no third accent hue is introduced. Each of the two brand hues is always used as a ramp (multiple tints/shades within one surface), never as a single flat swatch standing alone.

rules.name: The Orange-Is-Focus Rule
rules.body: Orange marks the single thing the user is currently looking at or acting on (centered node, hover, active nav link, rating). It never marks a merely-related or structural element — that's blue's job.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Inter is the only typeface in the system across every weight and role; no serif or display face is introduced for headings.

rules.name: The Tinted-Shadow Rule
rules.body: No shadow in the system is pure black; every shadow value carries either the blue-ink tint (rgba(23,29,51,...) / rgba(16,21,36,...)) or the orange-focus tint (rgba(229,114,0,...)), matching the element it lifts.

dos: Do treat orange as the single "you are here / active" marker and blue as the "structurally connected" marker; never swap their roles.
Do use full graduated ramps (50-800/900) for both brand hues rather than one flat swatch per hue.
Do tint every shadow toward blue-ink or orange-focus rgba values instead of pure black.
Do keep corners rounded system-wide: pill (999px) for badges/chips, 14-20px for cards and modals, 10px for buttons.
Do reserve the deep-blue-to-white-to-orange gradient (major/field/code) navigation pattern for hierarchical drill-down breadcrumbs like Explore's tier bar.
donts: Don't introduce a third accent hue; every color must trace back to the orange ramp, the blue ramp, or the gray neutral scale.
Don't use sharp/unrounded corners on cards, buttons, or badges — no element in the shipped system uses a 0px radius.

Don't assume Home or Login already carry this system — as of this build they are unstyled/placeholder and are not evidence of an alternate direction; they are pending adoption, not an exception to it.
